segments.heading: Warm things
segments.body: The kettle, the toaster and the oven all make things warm, and each one keeps that heat after it is switched off. Warm is not the same as safe: a just-boiled kettle looks the same as a cold one, and the steam above it is hotter than the water. That is why every warm thing in this kitchen is a grown-up's job, and why the child points at it and says what it is instead of touching it.
segments.short: The kettle, the toaster and the oven make things warm; ask your grown-up first.

segments.heading: Try it yourself
segments.body: Have the child fill the kettle at the sink, switch it on, and then touch the side of it to feel the warmth rise. The child should hold the handle only, watch the steam, and say out loud whether the side feels warm or cold before and after it boils. If it feels warm, the child says 'warm' and steps back one pace so the parent can pour.
segments.short: Fill the kettle and switch it on, then touch the side for warmth.

worked_example.short: Point, say warm, then point at the fridge and say cold.

learner_explanation: Look around the kitchen and name one warm and one cold thing.

stimulus.prompt: Ask the child to name one warm and one cold thing.
